scale: Levels 1 to 4. Each anchor describes what the interviewer saw or heard. Pick the highest level whose anchor the evidence matches in full.
hire_bar: No dimension at level 1. At least two dimensions at level 3 or above.

dimensions.name: Code change and testing
dimensions.signal: Makes a small change in an unfamiliar codebase, with tests, and explains the choices.
questions: Add the feature described in the task brief to the sample service.
How do you know the change works? Show it.

levels.1: Did not reach a running change in the time. Wrote no test, or tests that do not run.
levels.2: Reached a running change with help on the layout of the codebase. Tested the main path only. Named no edge case without a prompt.
levels.3: Reached a running change without help. Wrote tests for the main path and at least one edge case. Explained one trade-off in the change when asked.
levels.4: As level 3, and found a defect or a missing case in the existing code or the brief, said so, and proposed a fix or a question for the owner.

dimensions.name: System design
dimensions.signal: Turns a loose requirement into a design with stated limits, trade-offs and failure handling.
questions: Design a service that sends notifications to the users of a web app. Start with the questions you would ask.
What breaks first when the traffic grows ten times?

levels.1: Drew components before asking about requirements. Named no limit of the design when asked.
levels.2: Asked about requirements, then drew a design with one main path. Named failure cases only when prompted.
levels.3: Asked about load, data and failure requirements first. Gave a design with stated limits and one trade-off for each main choice. Named how the design fails and how it recovers.
levels.4: As level 3, and changed the design when a new constraint came up, with the cost of the change. Named what to measure to know the design works in production.

dimensions.name: Operating in production
dimensions.signal: Has run a service in production and describes an incident with the facts of what happened and what changed after it.
questions: Tell me about a production incident you worked on. What was your part?
What changed after it, and how did you check that the change worked?

levels.1: Gave no example of production work, or an example with no detail on their own actions.
levels.2: Described an incident in general terms. Their own actions stayed vague under follow-up questions. Named no change after the incident.
levels.3: Described an incident with a timeline, their own actions and the cause. Named a change that followed and who owned it.
levels.4: As level 3, and described how they checked that the change worked, with a measure or a test. Named what they would do another way with what they know now.

dimensions.name: Collaboration and feedback
dimensions.signal: Works through a disagreement with a colleague, and gives and takes feedback on work.
questions: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a technical decision on your team. What did you do?
Tell me about feedback on your work that changed how you work.

levels.1: Gave no example, or described the other person only as wrong, with no detail of what was said or done.
levels.2: Gave an example where someone else settled the disagreement, with little on their own actions.
levels.3: Gave an example with their own actions: stated their view, asked for the other view, and named the outcome and what they did after it.
levels.4: As level 3, and described a case where they changed their own view on evidence, or changed how they work after feedback, with what changed.
